verdict.line: You lose if you let him stack Grog-Soaked Blade poison in extended melee trades; you win by poking with ranged Cannon form and punishing his all-in cooldowns.

brief.thesis: This is a 47.5% head-to-head over 3358 games because both champions are trade-pattern champions with no hard CC, so the lane is decided by who controls the range gap, not by a mechanical mismatch. Jayce in Cannon Stance can out-range Parrrley's 625-range poke, but every time you swap to Hammer Stance to melee or finish a trade you step into his autoattack poison and give up your range advantage.

theirWindow.when: you are stuck in melee Hammer Stance
theirWindow.what: Gangplank's autos apply Grog-Soaked Blade poison that ramps with level, and he can land free Parrrley pokes at 625 range while you're not using Cannon Stance to answer. If you're forced into Hammer form to finish a kill, expect stacking poison damage over the next few seconds.

yourWindow.when: after he uses Q (Parrrley) on minions/you
yourWindow.what: Parrrley is on a 5s cooldown, so right after he fires it he has no ranged poke for several seconds. Swap to Cannon Stance and fire Shock Blast through an Acceleration Gate (E) or just at full charge to punish the window before he can reset.

start.why: Doran's Blade is the 89.6%-pick start (46.6% win rate over 3503 games) because the extra AD and sustain let you trade autos in Cannon Stance without losing the poke war to his Parrrley.

boots.why: Plated Steelcaps are the higher-win-rate boots pick (47.9% over 1653 games) and reduce the physical damage from both his autoattacks and Parrrley, which matters since his poison and Q are both physical over time.

core.why: Builds mana for Muramana scaling and sustains your Cannon Stance poke pattern without running dry.
The active haste lets you dash in with Q (To the Skies!) to punish his cooldowns and disengage before his autos stack poison.
Converts your mana into burst damage, letting you win short trades before he can land enough autos to ramp Grog-Soaked Blade.
The 21.3%-pick path to this item has the best measured win rate (53.9% over 586 games), adding burst that punishes his melee engages.

situational.when: he builds armor or tankiness to soak your pokes
his team has burst or hard engage you need to shield through

runes.keystoneWhy: The Sorcery page (24.8% pick, 46.9% win rate) rewards you for staying mobile and poking rather than standing in melee range, which directly counters his autoattack poison stacking.

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite is the most-picked combo (57% pick, 47.3% win rate) and the Ignite lets you close out short trade windows before he can Remove Scurvy heal back the damage.

playing.title: Stay in Cannon Stance by default
playing.detail: Cannon Stance's Shock Blast matches his Parrrley's 625 range, so defaulting to ranged form denies him free pokes and avoids exposing you to his autoattack poison.

playing.title: Punish the 5s Parrrley cooldown
playing.detail: Every time he fires Q (Parrrley), he has no ranged tool for 5 seconds. Use that window to land a Shock Blast or push a short trade.

playing.title: Use E (Acceleration Gate) before engaging
playing.detail: Deploy the gate and fire Shock Blast through it for increased missile speed, range, and damage, letting you land pokes from further away than his Parrrley can punish.

playing.title: Avoid stacking poison in extended fights
playing.detail: Grog-Soaked Blade's poison damage increases with level, so swap back to Cannon Stance after any Hammer Stance engage rather than staying in melee range.

playing.title: Track his Remove Scurvy cooldown (18-22s)
playing.detail: His W clears CC and heals him, so time your E (Thundering Blow) knockback or all-in burst for when you've seen him use it recently and it's still down.

playing.title: Respect Cannon Barrage from level 6
playing.detail: His ultimate has global range and deals damage over time while slowing, so don't overextend in lane once he hits level 6, even if the direct trade looks winning.

playing.title: Hold R (Mercury Cannon) for extended trades
playing.detail: Transforming reduces his armor on your first attack, which matters most once you've committed to a longer fight rather than a quick poke exchange.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and win rates above are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning and trade-window advice are my own tactical read of the matchup.

stats.opponentTip: Destroy his Powder Kegs (E) to win combat. Be careful of his Grasp of the Undying stacks while maintaining your distance from him.
